summary: Describes an MGCP package for handling endpoints stuck in a lockstep state, in which events are quarantined but not reported, for example after a Call Agent failover during a transient call.

plainLanguage.summary: This MGCP extension lets an endpoint report that it has been stuck waiting too long. A timer triggers a message to the Call Agent if the endpoint remains in lockstep.

questions: how does the lck timer work
what does an mgcp lockstep report do
subtitle: A timer-based way for MGCP endpoints to report a prolonged lockstep state.

tldr.problem: An MGCP endpoint may remain in lockstep after a failure and stop processing events without the Call Agent knowing.
tldr.mechanism: The LCK package lets a Call Agent set a timer; if it expires, the endpoint sends RestartInProgress with the lockstep method.
tldr.outcome: The package provides a way to report the stuck condition so a Call Agent can take recovery steps.

today: RFC 3992 is an Informational document describing an MGCP package. The IESG note says MGCP is non-IETF and identifies RFC 3015 as the standards-based approach to the same needs.

sections.title: When an Endpoint Is in Lockstep
sections.content:
In MGCP step mode, an endpoint that sends a Notify waits for a response and then for a new NotificationRequest before resuming event processing. The RFC calls this waiting condition the lockstep state.

Normally the endpoint should remain there only briefly. An adverse failure, such as a Call Agent failover during a transient call, can leave it unable to process events or notify the new Call Agent.
sections.plainLanguage: An endpoint waits for a reply and a new instruction before processing more events. If the controller changes during a failure, the endpoint can stay stuck without telling the new controller.

sections.title: The LCK Timer and Report
sections.content:
The RFC defines the Lockstep package, named LCK, version 0. A Call Agent configures the LCK/LST parameter with a time in seconds from 0 to 9999; zero turns reporting off.

If the endpoint remains in lockstep until the timer expires, it sends RestartInProgress with the LCK/lockstep restart method. The timer is cancelled if the endpoint leaves lockstep first.
sections.plainLanguage: The Call Agent sets how long the endpoint may wait before reporting. If the timer runs out, the endpoint sends a message saying it is in lockstep.

sections.title: Security and Protocol Context
sections.content:
The RFC says the base MGCP security requirements also apply to this package. It requires a security protocol such as IPsec to provide per-message authentication and integrity, so the parties can verify message sources and detect modification.

An IESG note identifies MGCP as a non-IETF protocol and points implementers to RFC 3015 as the standards-based way to meet the needs MGCP was designed to address.
sections.plainLanguage: Messages need authentication and integrity protection so endpoints and Call Agents can trust them. The IESG note points to RFC 3015 as the standards-based alternative.
